title: RADIAN@: Regime-Adaptive Dilated Inter-Attention Network for Non-Stationary Financial Time-Series Forecasting
content: Financial forecasting is challenged by non-stationarity, volatility clustering, and regime transitions, which can degrade model generalization under distribution shift. Existing neural forecasting architectures often combine expressive encoders with static decoder mappings, limiting their ability to adapt to changing market conditions. This paper introduces RADIAN, a forecasting architecture that preserves regime-agnostic representation learning while applying causal regime conditioning exclusively within its fusion and decoding modules. The conditioning signal is a four-dimensional regime vector derived from normalized one-step target returns over the input window. RADIAN is evaluated on nine hourly financial datasets spanning multiple asset classes and compared against eight competitive baselines using a fixed experimental protocol and three random seeds. Across the datasets, RADIAN achieves the lowest mean test mean absolute error (MAE), with an average improvement of 0.67% over the strongest baseline on each dataset. Statistical analyses indicate significant improvements with large paired effect sizes, while ablation studies identify decoder-side regime conditioning as the primary contributor to robustness under non-stationary market dynamics.
